title: When Can an AI Agent Serve as a Model of Human Psychopathology?
abstract: arXiv:2611.28405v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Language models and AI agents are increasingly described in psychiatric terms, such as anxious, depressed, addicted or helpless. A recent study even proposed language models as experimental systems for psychiatry and as a platform for piloting psychological treatments. We ask when an experiment on an AI agent can provide evidence about a specified human psychiatric process. A claim to such evidence has three parts. Something changed in the agent, and the agent's history caused the change. Nothing other than a process shared with people explains that change. The change matches one theory of the human process and not that theory's rivals. Psychiatry and its neighbouring fields have an evidence standard for each part, from the diagnostic manuals' rule for induced states, from clinical test scores and from animal models. translated_title: AI智能体何时能够作为人类精神病理学的模型？
translated_abstract: 语言模型和AI智能体越来越多地被用精神病学术语来描述，例如焦虑的、抑郁的、成瘾的或无助的。最近的一项研究甚至提出将语言模型作为精神病学的实验系统，以及试运行心理治疗的平台。我们探讨的是，对AI智能体的实验何时能够为特定的人类精神病理过程提供证据。这类证据主张包含三个部分：智能体中发生了某种变化，且智能体的历史导致了这种变化；除了与人类共享的某种过程之外，没有其他因素能够解释这种变化；这种变化符合关于人类过程的某一种理论，而不符合与其竞争的理论。精神病学及其邻近领域为每个部分都设有证据标准，分别来自诊断手册中关于诱发状态的规则、临床测试分数以及动物模型。我们将这些标准逐一转化为机器研究可以满足的准则。对于语言模型而言，最关键的替代……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文将精神病学及其相关领域的证据标准转化为AI实验可满足的具体准则，用以判定何时对AI智能体的实验能够真正为特定的人类精神病理过程提供科学证据。
en_tdlr: This paper translates evidence standards from psychiatry and its neighboring fields into criteria that machine studies can meet, determining when experiments on AI agents can provide valid evidence about specified human psychiatric processes.
